buildSteps.title: Generate quantum states
buildSteps.detail: A laser produces either weak coherent pulses or entangled photon pairs in a nonlinear crystal.

buildSteps.title: Encode the key
buildSteps.detail: Each photon is prepared in one of several bases, for example polarisation or phase, representing a random bit.

buildSteps.title: Transmit through the channel
buildSteps.detail: Photons travel through optical fibre or free space to the receiver; losses and noise must stay low enough for detection.

buildSteps.title: Detect and record
buildSteps.detail: Single-photon detectors at the receiver measure each photon and log the time and basis used.

buildSteps.title: Sift the raw key
buildSteps.detail: Sender and receiver compare, over an authenticated classical channel, which bases matched, discarding the rest.

buildSteps.title: Correct errors
buildSteps.detail: Classical error-correction algorithms reconcile the remaining discrepancies without revealing the key.

buildSteps.title: Amplify privacy
buildSteps.detail: The reconciled string is compressed to remove any information an eavesdropper might have gained, producing a shorter secret key.

buildSteps.title: Integrate with encryption
buildSteps.detail: The key is delivered to encryptors or key-management systems that use it for one-time pad or symmetric encryption.

prerequisites.why: they must reliably register individual photons with low noise and high timing resolution.
fibre at telecom wavelengths keeps photon loss low enough for links over tens of kilometres.
they would extend range without trusted nodes, but are still at laboratory-demonstration stage.
without authentication, an eavesdropper could impersonate the receiver and break the protocol.
entanglement-based protocols need reliable sources of correlated photon pairs.

pathway.milestone: point-to-point quantum key distribution links in metro networks and dedicated fibres
pathway.unlocks: high-security links for government, finance and critical infrastructure.
key distribution over city-to-city and intercontinental distances.
long-distance links without trusting intermediate nodes.
security based on minimal assumptions about the hardware.
